modern-classic.description: Out of production, 10–30 years old, enthusiast demand rising. Sold through enthusiast auctions and specialist dealers. Condition spread is huge — documentation decides value.
modern-classic.label: Modern classic (1995–2015)

new.description: Cars you can buy new today. Price means MSRP minus incentives plus dealer markup on hot models. Best price comes from comparing dealer quotes, not list price.
new.label: New & current models

used.description: In production recently or just out of it. Deep listing inventory everywhere — best price is a search problem, solved by aggregation and patience.
used.label: Used modern (2015–today)

vintage.description: Pre-1995 and collector-grade. Auction results set the market; provenance and matching numbers outweigh mileage. Buy expertise before you buy the car.
vintage.label: Vintage & collector (pre-1995)

channels.blurb: The auction site that reset modern-classic pricing. Every sale is public, so its results archive is the market's memory — the single best price reference for 1980s–2010s enthusiast cars.
channels.name: Bring a Trailer

channels.blurb: Doug DeMuro's auction platform for 1980s-and-newer enthusiast cars, with the same public-results transparency as BaT and lower fees for sellers.
channels.name: Cars & Bids

channels.blurb: The largest collector-car auction house in the world by volume — televised, fast, and the price-setter for American muscle and classics.
channels.name: Mecum Auctions

channels.blurb: The top of the market. Pebble Beach and Monterey headline sales; if a car trades here, its result is the record the whole market cites.
channels.name: RM Sotheby's

channels.blurb: Centuries-old auction house with deep European coverage — Goodwood sales and classic grids that BaT doesn't reach.
channels.name: Bonhams Motoring

channels.blurb: The classified bible of the American classic-car hobby since 1954. If it's old and for sale in the US, it's probably listed here.
channels.name: Hemmings

channels.blurb: One of the largest US listing aggregators — dealer new inventory plus used, with pricing tools that flag above/below market.
channels.name: AutoTrader

channels.blurb: Best-in-class deal ratings: every listing scored against market value, so overpriced cars identify themselves. Start used searches here.
channels.name: CarGurus

channels.blurb: Huge US inventory and a research side (reviews, comparisons) that makes it a solid one-stop for mainstream buying.
channels.name: Cars.com

channels.blurb: Buy entirely online with a 7-day return window. Prices run high versus private party, but the process is the simplest in used cars.
channels.name: Carvana

channels.blurb: Shows what others actually paid for the same car locally — the reference number to take into a dealership.
channels.name: TrueCar

channels.blurb: Where the cheap cars live. No buyer protection and no polish, but private-party prices beat dealer retail by thousands — bring a friend and a pre-purchase inspection.
channels.name: Facebook Marketplace

channels.blurb: Tesla, Rivian, and Lucid sell direct at posted prices — no negotiation, no dealer markup, and the configurator is the showroom.
channels.name: Manufacturer direct (Tesla / Rivian / Lucid)

note: Curated outbound destinations, wave 1. Car Atlas does not sell cars or take commissions on listings; channel blurbs are editorial. Always verify a listing on the destination site itself.

priceWatch.cadence: Refresh cycles target a 6-hour ingest per source, with per-listing timestamps shown on every record — a stale price is labeled stale, never presented as live.
priceWatch.design: Price Watch is specified in API.md and rolls out in waves: (1) listing ingest adapters per channel in buying.json, normalizing to a common schema (model slug, year, trim, mileage, location, price, source, first-seen, last-seen); (2) price history per listing and per model-year cohort; (3) drop detection against cohort medians; (4) opt-in alerts. Wave 1 ships the schema, the cohort-median method, and this design — no fabricated live prices anywhere.
priceWatch.stage1: Stage 1 shipped in wave 4 (2026-10-13): certified auction results in data/v1/price-watch.json, rendered on the Buy page and on the model pages they belong to. Listings ingest, cohorts, and alerts remain later stages.
priceWatch.stage2: Stage 2 shipped in wave 7 (2026-10-13): the certified-results set extended to the same standard — 19 results in all, each sourced and day-dated, with uncertifiable candidates recorded as skips in the file rather than approximated. Stage 2 is results ingest only; the listings ingest, cohorts, and alerts remain later stages.
priceWatch.stage3: Stage 3 shipped in wave 8 (2026-10-13): the certified-results set extended again to the same standard — 28 results in all, each sourced and day-dated, with one further uncertifiable candidate recorded as a skip in the file rather than approximated. Stage 3 is results ingest only; the listings ingest, cohorts, and alerts remain later stages.
priceWatch.stage4: Stage 4 shipped in wave 9 (2026-10-13): the certified-results set extended a third time to the same standard — 37 results in all, each sourced and day-dated, with one further uncertifiable candidate recorded as a skip in the file rather than misattributed. Stage 4 is results ingest only; the listings ingest, cohorts, and alerts remain later stages.
